paragraphs.text: Freeze-casting is a shaping route for porous ceramics. This SYNTHETIC paper studies an alumina scaffold, denoted sample AL-P1, produced by freeze-casting an aqueous alumina slurry.

Sample AL-P1 was cast from a slurry with a solid loading of 20 vol%, which this synthetic paper claims to be the optimal loading, and was then sintered in air at 1250 °C. The dwell time at the sintering temperature is not reported in this synthetic source.
The total porosity of sample AL-P1, measured by the Archimedes method, was 42 %. The pore channels were aligned along the freezing direction.

sources.title: SYNTHETIC PAPER P1: Freeze-cast alumina scaffolds sintered at low temperature

paragraphs.text: This SYNTHETIC paper reports an alumina membrane, denoted sample AL-S1, prepared by freeze-casting. Sample AL-S1 is a physically distinct specimen with a different slurry formulation from any earlier synthetic sample.
Sample AL-S1 was sintered in air at 1350 °C. The optimal solid loading claimed in this synthetic paper is 30 vol%.
The total porosity of sample AL-S1, measured by mercury intrusion porosimetry, was 38 %. No mechanical strength data are reported in this synthetic source.

sources.title: SYNTHETIC PAPER S1: Freeze-cast alumina membranes for filtration
